findings.title: Negative-offset branch slices the queryset with a negative start, which Django rejects
findings.description: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code assigns `start_offset = cursor.offset` and runs `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django querysets do not support negative indexing and raise an error on negative slice bounds, so this branch fails on every request that reaches it. The comment says it "enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds," but the slice never produces that result. The `start_offset = cursor.offset` line is also redundant with the `else` path's logic. I did not open the file to confirm the Django version, so this rests on the standard queryset slicing behavior.

findings.title: BasePaginator comment says negative offsets are allowed, but the code clamps them to zero
findings.description: The new comment says the change "allow[s] negative offsets," but `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` clamps negative offsets to 0 for forward cursors. For `is_prev` cursors, a negative `offset` is passed straight into `queryset[offset:stop]`, which Django rejects. The comment's claim that "the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions" is false for that path. The `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check on the following lines also still uses the unclamped `offset`, so it no longer matches the slice that was actually taken.

findings.title: Cursor and paginator comments describe behavior the code does not implement
findings.description: The comment added above `self.offset = int(offset)` says it enables "efficient reverse pagination from arbitrary positions in large datasets," but the line only casts the value to `int`. Nothing in this diff makes negative offsets efficient or supported. The `OptimizedCursorPaginator` docstring and comments in `paginator.py` repeat similar unsupported claims, such as "Negative offset support for efficient reverse pagination" and "Streamlined boundary condition handling."

findings.title: Superusers and global-access members can request out-of-bounds pagination through an opt-in query flag
findings.description: `enable_advanced` is true for any superuser or any member with `has_global_access`. Setting `?optimized_pagination=true` then routes the request to the paginator with negative offsets enabled. The comment justifies this by saying "permissions are checked at the queryset level," but this diff does not show that check, and the endpoint's own queryset is not visible in the hunk. The feature is also undocumented and has no tests in this diff. Before shipping, confirm that the negative-offset path cannot return rows the caller is not authorized to see.

findings.title: `organization_context.member` is dereferenced without a None check
findings.description: `request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access` only avoids the attribute access when the user is a superuser. If `organization_context.member` can be `None` for a non-superuser who passes `OrganizationAuditPermission`, this raises `AttributeError`. I did not verify whether the permission class guarantees a membership object, so this is informational.
